transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-21
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Alicia Park (Redwood AE), Tom Nguyen (Redwood SE), Jared Kim (Redwood CSM), Raj Patel (Mistral CTO), Leah Ortiz (Mistral SRE), Eric Simmons (Mistral Head of AI), Nora Diaz (Mistral Procurement)

Summary:
Quick renewal check-in focused on adding EU region nodes, clarifying Dedicated vs hosted with VPC-onboarding, and aligning procurement timeline. Mistral wants a small private pilot benchmark before committing to a 12-month Dedicated uplift. Security and KMS options are gating items.

Topics discussed:
- Capacity uplift quantities and burst windows
- EU region provisioning timeline and residency
- VPC/private deployment vs Dedicated hosted tradeoffs
- Security: SOC2 artifacts, KMS/HSM, audit logs
- Pricing cadence and contract amendment process

Action items (recap at end) included pricing, booking benchmark, and procurement timeline.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alicia Park: hey everyone thanks for joining, we wanted to do a short check-in on the renewal and the region provisioning. how's the week?
[00:16] Raj Patel: hey thanks Alicia, busy but good. we've reviewed the usage numbers from last quarter and looks like we need more headroom for model stepping into production.
[00:28] Tom Nguyen: quick context from our side, we saw the spike in token throughput on the fine-tuned recommender, so the capacity conversation makes sense. curious about expected p95 latency targets for EU hosts?
[00:42] Eric Simmons: ideally under 200ms p95 for 512 token requests, that's our internal goal. cost is also material, we can't 4x the bill.
[00:56] Leah Ortiz: and from ops, network egress and VPC peering need a clean path. we also want KMS integration because of regulatory logs retention.
[01:10] Alicia Park: absolutely, so two things: for EU we can provision Dedicated capacity in the EU-west region and we also support Private VPC deployment if you need customer-managed networking. there are latency wins with local nodes and also some cost differences.
[01:26] Raj Patel: can you remind me the difference in billing for Dedicated vs Private VPC? i always mix those.
[01:35] Alicia Park: sure, dedicated is reserved GPU pools we provision and bill as committed monthly capacity; private is the same serving runtime but with your VPC and control plane segregation — usually there's an enterprise fee for the private control plane plus provisioning costs. Tom, feel free to add on the infra side.
[01:52] Tom Nguyen: yeah to add, private VPC can have slightly higher ops overhead and a small platform add-on; latency is comparable if we colocate nodes in your region. Dedicated hosted (Redwood-managed) is faster to start and lower upfront ops. also note we can do hybrid — pin sensitive workloads to private and burst to dedicated.
[02:12] Nora Diaz: procurement question — what contract term options do you offer for a capacity top-up? we prefer annual but might do 6-month pilots.
[02:21] Alicia Park: standard is 12-month commits for best unit pricing, but we can do a 3-month pilot amendment and then roll into 12 months. pricing table i'll send after this call.
[02:32] Eric Simmons: about the pilot — we want a short benchmark to validate p95 and throughput under our workload. can you run a private pilot in our VPC or do you need a hosted pilot?
[02:44] Tom Nguyen: we can run a private pilot in your VPC — we typically ask for an hour-long window where we replay representative traffic, collect latency, token-cost metrics, and kv-cache hit rates. we'll need an infra contact and a few allowed IPs.
[03:00] Leah Ortiz: ok that sounds reasonable. we'll need the runbook and network CIDR list.
[03:09] Alicia Park: i'll attach a runbook. Tom will set the test. Raj, who should be our technical contact?
[03:16] Raj Patel: Leah will own ops side, Eric will validate model-level metrics, and Nora will coordinate contractual items.
[03:24] Tom Nguyen: noted. also a quick note on quantization: if you want to save token-costs we can recommend a q4_0 profile for the recommender; it reduces GPU memory and cost but we should validate accuracy drift in your eval set.
[03:40] Eric Simmons: that's important — don't want quality regression. can we include an eval pass in the pilot?
[03:45] Tom Nguyen: yes, include a small eval harness. we'll capture rouge/accuracy deltas during the spike tests.
[03:52] Raj Patel: security gating: we need SOC2 type II report, KMS support (we prefer AWS KMS but could use our HSM), and audit log exports to our SIEM. do you provide those artifacts?
[04:05] Alicia Park: yes SOC2 is available, we'll include the latest attestation. for KMS we support both Redwood-managed keys via cloud KMS and customer KMS integrations; for HSM we have an enterprise onboarding path — i'll include the security package with the KMS options. audit logs are exportable to your S3 or SIEM via syslog.
[04:25] Nora Diaz: for contract terms we have two blocking items: indemnity language around data residency and a clear SLA clause for latency and availability.
[04:35] Alicia Park: we can propose SLA targets and define availability windows; indemnity is something our legal team will review and we can mark those as exceptions in the amendment. i'll loop in legal once we have the procurement timeline.
[04:47] Raj Patel: timeline wise, we'd like to be on Dedicated EU nodes by the end of november if possible, but that depends on procurement and the pilot results.
[04:57] Alicia Park: that feels doable if we run the pilot the week of Oct 27 and you approve the PO the following week. so proposed milestones: pilot week Oct 27, finalize pricing and contract by Oct 30, provision EU nodes first week of November, and go-live by end of November. does that match your constraints?
[05:17] Leah Ortiz: that timeline is tight but feasible. need to confirm IP allow-list and KMS choice by Oct 25.
[05:25] Eric Simmons: also confirm expected throughput — we requested an uplift from 200 rps to 600 rps peak; will provisioning be elastic or fixed?
[05:35] Tom Nguyen: Dedicated can be reserved for baseline 400 rps and autoscale burst to 600 for short windows; we can size the pool accordingly. autoscaling policies and burst configs will be in the proposal.
[05:47] Raj Patel: curious about fallback — if EU capacity spikes beyond our reserved pool do you automatically route to non-EU nodes? that's a data residency question.
[05:57] Alicia Park: good point. routing policies can be set by you: strict residency (fail if no EU capacity) or soft fallback to other regions; we usually recommend soft fallback for critical uptime but for regulated workloads we can lock to EU only. we'll document options.
[06:14] Nora Diaz: procurement: what's the lead time for amendment once we sign? and is there an onboarding fee for VPC?
[06:22] Alicia Park: amendment lead time is normally 5 business days for our contracts team to prepare. there is a one-time private control plane setup fee for VPC onboarding — i'll include the exact number in the pricing doc.
[06:34] Tom Nguyen: from ops — to minimize onboarding time, share your network diagram and KMS contact; we'll prepare IaC snippets for peering.
[06:44] Leah Ortiz: will you provide templates for peering? we use terraform.
[06:48] Tom Nguyen: yes we provide Terraform snippets and a checklist for required security groups, routes, and NAT config.
[06:54] Raj Patel: any competitors we should be worried about? i know A- team Aurora AI pitched multi-region but their latency numbers were fuzzy.
[07:02] Alicia Park: noted — Aurora AI and CloudProbe come up in RFPs. we differentiate on the unified runtime and tooling for rollouts, plus transparent token-level cost.
[07:12] Eric Simmons: okay last question on observability — what dashboards do you give? we need per-route latency, token-cost breakdown, and error traces tied to prompts.
[07:23] Tom Nguyen: Redwood console provides per-model and per-route dashboards, trace hooks, and raw request/response logs for the pilot. retention windows vary by plan; we'll include a retention add-on.
[07:34] Alicia Park: great, i think we have clear next steps. quick recap: i'll send pricing + security pack, Tom will schedule the pilot and share runbook, Raj/Leah confirm network and KMS choice, Nora sends procurement timing.
[07:48] Raj Patel: thanks — sounds good. can you also include an expected cost estimate for the 12-month committed uplift so procurement has a ballpark?
[07:58] Alicia Park: yes i'll include a committed pricing scenario and a pilot-only cost scenario.
[08:05] Nora Diaz: and please flag any long lead items in the contract, like export controls or bespoke indemnity.
[08:13] Alicia Park: will do.
[08:17] Jared Kim: i'll follow up on the account side and ensure crm notes are updated and link the security pack.
[08:24] Eric Simmons: ok thanks everyone.
[08:27] Alicia Park: thanks all, we'll follow up with the documents and propose the pilot window.
[08:32] Raj Patel: thanks. bye.

End of call.

Recap / Final notes:
- Pilot approach: 1-hour private VPC benchmark; capture p95 latency, throughput, kv-cache hit rates, and eval accuracy deltas.
- Security pack: SOC2, KMS options (customer KMS/HSM support), audit log export methods.
- Proposed timeline: pilot week Oct 27, pricing/contract by Oct 30, EU provisioning in first week of Nov, go-live by end of Nov (dependent on PO).
- Procurement asks: confirm IP ranges, KMS choice, legal indemnity points; procurement to provide timeline/PO by Oct 29.

Attachments referenced (links to be posted in CRM): runbook, Terraform snippets, pricing draft, SOC2 attestation, KMS integration guide.
